To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a cDNA clone encoding a mimotope of the tandem repeat epitope of the breast mucin.
we have cloned a pS2 mRNA cDNA that encodes an alternate reading frame that is a mimotope of the tandem repeat of human breast epithelium mucin.

we have isolated a cDNA clone that encodes a 44 amino-acid protein that is a mimotope of the Mc5 epitopic sequence of the breast mucin and that this cDNA clone can be expressed in high levels in E.coli.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the isolation of cDNA clones encoding a breast epithelial cell surface antigen, the development of a sensitive assay for the detection of the antigen, and with the identification of the epitopes recognized by the anti-breast epithelial cell surface antibodies.
the development of monoclonal antibodies and mimotopes for the detection of breast cancer.
the isolation, characterization and production of the NP5 fusion protein and the development of a diagnostic assay for mucin in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NP5 cDNAs encode a protein that is a mimic of breast epithelial mucins.
we have identified a cDNA clone that encodes a protein that is a mimotope of the breast epithelial mucins.

the NP5 cDNAs encode a 44 amino-acid protein that is a mimotope of a breast mucin epitope and that this cDNA has been used to develop a sensitive assay for breast mucin derived epitopes in patient serum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NP5 cDNAs are a new class of breast mucin mimotopes and that they can be expressed to high levels in E. coli.
the pS2 cDNA has a novel immunogenic epitope that is a mimotope for breast mucin.
the mucin tandem repeat is a major epitope for breast mucin and that a mimotope of this epitope can be expressed in bacteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NP5 cDNAs encode a 44 amino protein that has no homology with any known protein but has 97% identity to the pS2 cDNA.
a mimotope of the tandem repeat can be produced in E. coli.
the mucin tandem repeat mimotope is not the major antigen recognized by the Mc5 antibody, and that a fusion protein can be used to detect mucin derived antigens in serum.
